celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالْعَادِيَاتِ﴾: the horses that run on raids and pant ﴿ضَبْحًا﴾: it is the sound of their insides when they run,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿فَالْمُورِيَاتِ﴾: the horses that strike fire ﴿قَدْحًا﴾ with their hooves when they travel by night over stony ground,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فَالْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحًا﴾: the horses that raid the enemy at the time of morning, through the raiding of their riders,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَأَثَرْنَ﴾: stirred up ﴿بِهِ﴾ — in the place of their running, or at that time — ﴿نَقْعًا﴾: dust, by the vigour of their movement,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ﴾ — with the dust — ﴿جَمْعًا﴾ of the enemy, that is, came into its midst. The verb is conjoined to the noun because [the noun] is to be interpreted as a verb, that is: "by those [fem.] that ran, then struck fire, then raided."

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾, the disbeliever, ﴿لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾: ungrateful, denying His blessing, Exalted is He,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ﴾, that is, his ingratitude, ﴿لَشَهِيدٌ﴾: he bears witness against himself through what he does,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ﴾, that is, wealth, ﴿لَشَدِيدٌ﴾, that is, intense in love of it, so he is miserly with it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ﴾: is stirred up and brought out ﴿مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ﴾ of the dead, that is, they are resurrected,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَحُصِّلَ﴾: is made clear and set apart ﴿مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ﴾: the hearts, of disbelief and faith,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ﴾: knowing, so He will recompense them for their disbelief. The pronoun refers back in the plural in view of the meaning of «الإنسان». This clause indicates the object of «يعلم», that is: "that We will recompense him at the time mentioned." «خبير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يومئذ», while He, Exalted is He, is always aware, because it is the Day of recompense.
